From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>

Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme.example>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Technical kickoff workshop — scheduling, agenda & pre-read

Sam / Priya —

Thanks again for agreeing to a POC with Redwood. We want to run a focused hands-on kickoff where we:
- Walk through the prompt routing and function-calling approach for your workflows
- Validate token-level routing and KV cache behavior with sample prompts
- Run a light load test (steady-state 50 TPS for 10m) to estimate throughput and latencies

Proposed slots (PT):
- Tue Jul 14, 10:00–11:30
- Wed Jul 15, 14:00–15:30
- Thu Jul 16, 09:00–10:30

If none of those work, share a few alternatives or use my booking link: https://calendly.com/redwood-inference/poc-kickoff-30m (I can expand to 90m once we lock a slot).

Attached is a short POC-overview.pdf. Before the session it would be great if you could:
- Send 1–2 representative prompt examples (with expected responses)
- Flag any IP/data restrictions for the session (we can route traffic to a private VPC if needed)

I’ll draft a concise agenda and a one-page prep checklist once you confirm a best slot.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: POC-overview.pdf

Hi Dev —

Thanks — Wed Jul 15 14:00 PT works for our team. We prefer a 90-minute working session and can join with product + infra folks.

Quick asks from our side:
- Can you include a short block for prompt review and templating?
- We want to see routing behavior when we include a low-confidence fallback to a smaller model.
- For the load test, 50 TPS sounds fine — we’ll validate on our staging endpoint.

I’ll attach a pair of prompts (customer_support_1.txt & summarization_sample.txt) later today.

Best,
Sam
Senior Product Manager, Acme Corp

Perfect — locking Wed Jul 15 14:00–15:30 PT. Calendar invite to follow.

Draft agenda (attached as kickoff-agenda.pdf) — please review and tell me if we should reorder or expand any section:
1) 14:00–14:10 — Introductions & success criteria (Acme + Redwood)
2) 14:10–14:35 — Prompt review & templating (we’ll annotate best-effort replacements)
3) 14:35–14:55 — Routing: model selection rules and fallback policies (Marissa)
4) 14:55–15:10 — Load test plan and metrics to capture (Sergio)
5) 15:10–15:25 — Run short smoke tests / sample prompt walk-through (joint)
6) 15:25–15:30 — Next steps and action items

Pre-read (one-pager): https://drive.google.com/file/d/1POC_PRE_READ (same folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cPOC-Acme-Kickoff)
Prep checklist (attached): prep-checklist.md — highlights: share sample prompts, open staging credentials, confirm list of participant emails, and any redaction rules.

Marissa / Sergio — can you each confirm the routing knobs and load-test checklist below are accurate before I send the calendar invite?

Routing knobs (Marissa):
- Per-route model pinning
- Confidence threshold for fallback (0.65 by default)
- Prefix caching enabled for repeated prompts

Load-test checklist (Sergio):
- Baseline latency capture (p50/p95/p99)
- Token consumption and cost estimate
- KV cache hit-rate measurement
- Rate-limited ramp (start 5 TPS -> 50 TPS over 5 minutes)

Thanks — I’ll circulate the invite once you confirm.

– Dev

Quick internal check-in then public reply — agreed with draft agenda. A couple of notes:
- For prompt templating, we’ll bring a short examples doc showing recommended token-reduction approaches (truncate unneeded context; prefer structured slots).
- Recommend lowering the fallback confidence to 0.6 for this POC so we exercise the smaller model more aggressively and observe degradation characteristics.

Sergio — can you confirm the ramp profile and that you’ll have the load harness ready? I’ll prepare a 5-slide deck for the routing demo.

Marissa
